_comment: Ruleset 1 of 5 — Protect main.
Apply with:  bash .github/branch-protection/apply.sh
Inspect with: gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/rulesets --jq '.[].name'
Remove with:  bash .github/branch-protection/apply.sh --remove
This uses the Rulesets API rather than the legacy branch-protection API
because it is the only one that can express 'require an approval from a
code owner' and 'require branches to be up to date' together, and because
it is what GitHub is actively developing.
The required status checks below are the exact job `name:` values emitted
by .github/workflows/ci.yml and .github/workflows/security.yml. Every one
of them runs unconditionally on every pull request and always reports a
conclusion, so none of them can deadlock a merge.
scripts/checks/check-rulesets.sh verifies that link mechanically: a context
named here that no workflow emits is a check that can never go green.
See docs/CI_CD.md §5 for the reasoning behind each rule.
'required_signatures' is deliberately NOT included. It is good practice,
but it requires every contributor to configure GPG or SSH commit signing,
which is a real barrier to a student's first contribution. It ships as an
opt-in file instead: optional/require-signed-commits.json.
CODEOWNERS routes reviews to the @Open-Source-Software-Club/technical-leads
and /core-team teams. A team named there must exist and have write access
to this repository, or the entry matches nothing — and combined with
'require_code_owner_review' that makes merges permanently impossible.
Approved pull requests are merged through a merge queue rather than by
the author keeping their branch up to date. Before the queue, 'require
branches to be up to date' plus 'dismiss stale reviews' meant every change
to main forced each approved pull request to be updated and re-approved
(#38 waited a week that way). The queue tests each pull request on top of
the latest main itself, so the strict up-to-date policy is off: the queue
is what guarantees it. Every required check must run on the `merge_group`
event, or queued pull requests wait until check_response_timeout_minutes.
